items.passage:
After a bit I grew easier again; he seemed to keep his equilibrium, and I looked out at the side window on the moon-flooded landscape, with some interest. I had never seen brighter moonlight.

Suddenly from out of the intense stillness and loneliness a figure, a human figure, became visible. It was that of a man, a young and active man, running along the footpath a few feet to our left, apparently from some whim, keeping pace with the fly. My first feeling was of satisfaction that I was no longer alone, at the tender mercies of my stupefied charioteer. But, as I gazed, a slight misgiving came over me. Who could it be running along this lonely road so late, and what was his motive in keeping up with us so steadily.
items.question: In the text, the running figure who keeps pace with the fly most likely symbolizes
options: the narrator's relief at reaching a familiar, well-traveled road
the driver's steady recovery of control over the carriage
a vague threat that turns the narrator's relief into unease
the narrator's own wish to leave the fly and walk home
items.explanation: 달빛 아래 고요와 외로움 속에서 나타난 인물은 처음엔 혼자가 아니라는 만족감을 주지만, 곧 왜 이렇게 늦게 따라오는지에 대한 불안을 일으킨다. 따라서 C가 그 인물이 안도를 불안으로 바꾸는 막연한 위협을 상징한다고 정확히 짚는다. A의 익숙한 길, B의 마부의 회복, D의 걸어가고 싶은 바람은 지문에 근거가 없다.

items.passage: There must always be Winter, there must always be night and storm and cold. It is then that the flowers rest--they cannot always be in bloom. But somewhere on the great world the sun is always shining, and, just so sure as you live, it will sometime shine on you. The dear God has made it so. There is so much sun and so much storm, and we must have our share of both. It is Winter in your heart now, but soon it will be Spring. You have had one long Summer, and there must be something in between. We are not different from all else the dear God has made. It is all in one law, as the Herr Doctor will tell you.
items.question: In the text, Winter most likely symbolizes
options: a season the speaker dreads because the flowers die forever
the cold climate the listener must leave in order to recover
a punishment sent to those who complain about their lives
a time of grief that will eventually give way to renewal
items.explanation: 화자는 꽃이 쉬는 시기로서 겨울을 말하고, 곧이어 너의 마음은 지금 겨울이지만 곧 봄이 올 것이라고 한다. 즉 겨울은 지나갈 슬픔의 시기를 상징하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 꽃이 영원히 죽는다고 하여 '쉰다'는 표현과 어긋나고, B와 C는 지문에 없는 내용이다.

items.passage:
The two first of these, however, have during the first fortnight of their vegetation the brown and golden hues of Autumn upon them.

But we must be more brief in our search after the beauties of May, or we shall not have space to name the half of them. Let us turn, then, towards our home inclosures; glancing, as we pass, at a few more of those sweet sights which belong to the fields exclusively. And first let us feed our eyes with the brilliant green of yonder Wheat-field. The stems, you see, have just attained height enough to wave gracefully in the wind; which, as it passes over them, seems to convert the whole into a beautiful lake of bright green undulating water.
items.question: In the text, the waving Wheat-field most likely symbolizes
options: the lively abundance and beauty that May brings to the fields
the brown and golden decline that marks the coming of Autumn
the damage that strong winds cause to young crops in spring
the writer's longing to leave the fields for a distant sea
items.explanation: 필자는 5월의 아름다움을 찾는 중이라고 밝히고, 밀밭의 선명한 초록이 바람에 물결쳐 아름다운 호수처럼 보인다고 묘사한다. 따라서 밀밭은 5월이 들판에 가져오는 생동감과 풍요로운 아름다움을 상징하므로 A가 정답이다. B의 갈색·금빛은 다른 식물에 대한 설명이고, C와 D는 지문에 근거가 없다.

items.passage:
The heavy, long-continued rains had made our trail extremely heavy, and in places almost impassable. The hours passed and we found ourselves advancing much more slowly than was desirable. The lowering clouds were massing on the mountain slopes, and the rain began to fall in torrents. It then began to dawn upon us that we might not be able to reach our destination in the limited time yet remaining of the fast-departing day.

Further progress along our dangerous path in the impenetrable gloom, that would immediately follow sunset, we knew to be impossible.
items.question: In the text, the impenetrable gloom that would follow sunset most likely symbolizes
options: the travelers' relief that the heavy rains had finally ended
an obstacle that threatens to halt the travelers' progress
the quiet beauty of the mountain scenery as evening falls
the travelers' growing distrust of the path they had chosen
items.explanation: 지문은 비와 진창 때문에 일행의 진행이 늦어지고, 해가 지면 곧 뚫을 수 없는 어둠이 와서 더 나아가는 것이 불가능하다고 말한다. 따라서 어둠은 여정을 멈추게 할 장애물을 상징하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 비가 오히려 쏟아지는 상황과 맞지 않고, C와 D는 지문에서 강조되지 않는다.

items.passage:
A penny, worth fifty times as much as a sovereign, was something to retain and treasure. Doubtless, in their jungle-lairs, the wise old gray-beards put their heads together and agreed to raise the price on pennies when the worthless gold was all worked off. Who could tell? Mayhap the strange white men could be made to give even twenty sticks for a priceless copper.

By the end of the week the trade went slack. There was only the slightest dribble of gold. An occasional penny was reluctantly disposed of for ten sticks, while several thousand dollars in silver came in.

On the morning of the eighth day no trading was done. The gray-beards had matured their plan and were demanding twenty sticks for a penny, One-Eye delivered the new rate of exchange.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “the slightest dribble of gold” most nearly suggests
options: a very small, irregular trickle of gold coming in
a sudden flood of gold arriving all at once
a quantity of gold that had been melted down
a store of gold that was being secretly hidden
items.explanation: 바로 앞 문장에서 거래가 시들해졌다고 하므로 이 구절은 금이 아주 조금씩만 들어오는 상황을 나타낸다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 정반대의 의미이고, C의 녹인 금과 D의 숨겨둔 금은 문맥과 관련이 없다.

items.passage: The day was gray and not warm, though it was the beginning of June, and a fire had been lighted in the study to serve the purpose, morally and physically, of the hot toddy recommended by the elder. Poor Mr. Buchanan spread his hands out to it when he was left alone. He was very much broken down. The tears came to his eyes. He felt forlorn, helpless, as if there was nothing in heaven or earth to support him. It was a question of money, and was not that a wretched thing to ask God for? The filthy siller, the root of so much evil. He could have demonstrated to you very powerfully, had you gone to ask his advice in such an emergency, that it was not money, but the love of money that was the root of all evil; but in his heart, in this dreadful emergency, he cursed it.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “very much broken down” most nearly suggests
options: badly injured in body after a recent fall
deeply discouraged and emotionally exhausted
furious with the elder who had advised him
weakened by an illness caught in the cold
items.explanation: 이어지는 문장에서 그는 눈물을 흘리고 쓸쓸하고 무력하며 의지할 데가 없다고 느낀다. 따라서 이 구절은 몸이 아니라 마음이 깊이 낙담하고 지친 상태를 뜻하므로 B가 정답이다. A와 D는 신체적 상태로 잘못 해석했고, C의 분노는 지문에 나타나지 않는다.

items.passage:
Not in contempt but to our sport inclined
Smile on us, shades of Judges short and tall
Portrayed on windows of the Temple Hall;
There was a time that ye grave thoughts resigned,
Then, warm with sack, the Serjeants' hearts waxed kind,
In mirth Lords Keepers danced the galliard all,
Not in contempt.

Of pleasures past the shadows here we find,
Gay strife on brighter swards we thus recall,
Where maiden laughter winged the flying ball;
Declare us, fair ones, with a merry mind
Not in contempt.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “maiden laughter winged the flying ball” most nearly suggests
options: the young women threw the ball in anger
birds carried the ball across the lawn
laughter seemed to lift and speed the ball
laughter interrupted and stopped the game
items.explanation: 이 구절은 지난날의 즐거운 놀이를 회상하는 맥락에 있으며, 웃음이 공에 날개를 달아준 듯하다는 비유이다. 따라서 웃음이 공을 들어 올려 빨리 날게 한 것 같다는 C가 정답이다. A의 분노와 D의 중단은 즐거운 분위기와 맞지 않고, B는 비유를 문자 그대로 읽은 오답이다.

items.passage: I believe that nowhere and at no time any such struggle can take place on a large scale unless each party is contending for something which has a great deal of truth in it. Where the right is plain, honest, wise, and noble-minded men are all on one side; and only rogues and fools are on the other. Where the wise and good are divided, the truth is generally found to be divided also. But this is precisely what cannot be admitted as long as the conflict continues. Men begin to fight about things when reason and argument fail to convince them.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “the truth is generally found to be divided also” most nearly suggests
options: the truth can never be known by anyone
only rogues and fools claim to hold the truth
the truth changes as a conflict goes on
each side holds part of what is right
items.explanation: 필자는 대규모 다툼은 각 편이 상당한 진실을 지닌 무언가를 위해 싸울 때만 일어난다고 말한다. 따라서 진실이 나뉜다는 것은 양측이 각각 옳은 부분을 일부씩 갖고 있다는 뜻이므로 D가 정답이다. A, B, C는 지문의 논지와 맞지 않는다.

items.passage:
I generally cover very great distances at a high speed without the least inconvenience to myself, but I find that those who accompany me nearly always break down.

After inspecting a number of applicants I fixed upon one man whose features showed firmness of character and unusual determination. He was a man of few words--one of the rarest and best qualities in a travelling servant, and--he had no relations dependent upon him--the next best quality. He could shoot straight, he could stick on a saddle, he could walk. He required little sleep. He was willing to go to any country where I chose to take him.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “he could stick on a saddle” most nearly suggests
options: he could ride well without being thrown
he knew how to mend a torn saddle
he disliked riding on long journeys
he preferred walking to riding a horse
items.explanation: 이 구절은 사격, 도보 같은 여행 하인으로서의 능력들과 나란히 나열되어 있다. 따라서 말에서 떨어지지 않고 잘 탈 수 있다는 A가 정답이다. B는 '안장'이라는 단어만 따온 오답이고, C와 D는 칭찬하는 문맥과 어긋난다.

items.passage:
Eva looked into the brook, and saw a tiny child standing between the Elves. “Now I can go with you,” said she, “but see, I can no longer step from the bank to yonder stone, for the brook seems now like a great river, and you have not given me wings like yours.”

But the Fairies took each a hand, and flew lightly over the stream. The Queen and her subjects came to meet her, and all seemed glad to say some kindly word of welcome to the little stranger. They placed a flower-crown upon her head, laid their soft faces against her own, and soon it seemed as if the gentle Elves had always been her friends.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “the brook seems now like a great river” most nearly suggests
options: the brook has flooded after a heavy rain
Eva has become so small that the brook looks huge
Eva has always been afraid of deep water
the brook flows on to join a distant river
items.explanation: 앞 문장에서 Eva는 시냇물 속에서 요정들 사이에 선 아주 작은 아이를 본다. 그녀가 작아졌기 때문에 시냇물이 큰 강처럼 보이는 것이므로 B가 정답이다. A의 홍수, C의 두려움, D의 실제 강은 지문에 근거가 없다.

items.passage:
Now and then one of those chill gusts of air, which seem to be careering about aimlessly in the atmosphere during early summer, would strike into his face, and recal! him to a keener self-consciousness.

Ralph concluded, from his increasing agitation, that he must be very near Bertha’s home. He stopped and looked around him. He saw a large maple at the roadside, some thirty steps from where he was standing, and the girl who was sitting under it, resting her head in her hand and gazing out over the sea, he recognized in an instant to be Bertha. He sprang up on the road, not crossing, however, her line of vision, and approached her ______ from behind.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: loudly
angrily
silently
carelessly
items.explanation: Ralph는 Bertha의 시야를 가로지르지 않으면서 뒤에서 다가가므로, 들키지 않게 조용히 다가간다는 말이 들어가야 한다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A와 D는 몰래 다가가려는 의도와 맞지 않고, B의 분노는 문맥에 없다.

items.passage:
Masouda took a key from her girdle, and, having looked around to see that they were alone, unlocked it.

“Enter,” she said, pushing them before her. They obeyed, and through the darkness within heard her close the door.

“Now we are ______ awhile,” she said with a sigh, “or, at least, so I think. But I will lead you to where there is more light.”

Then, taking each of them by the hand, she went forward along a smooth incline, till presently they saw the moonlight, and by it discovered that they stood at the mouth of a cave which was fringed with bushes. Running up from the depths of the gulf below to this opening was a ridge or shoulder of rock, very steep and narrow.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: lost
trapped
guilty
safe
items.explanation: Masouda는 주변에 아무도 없는지 확인한 뒤 문을 잠그고 들어와 한숨을 쉰다. 이어서 적어도 자신은 그렇게 생각한다고 덧붙이므로 잠시 안전하다는 뜻이 자연스럽고 D가 정답이다. A와 B는 안도하는 한숨과 맞지 않고, C는 문맥과 무관하다.

items.passage: There was an old goose, which they kept as the guardian of their humble cottage; and they bethought them to make this a sacrifice in honor of their guests. But the goose, too ______, with the aid of feet and wings, for the old folks, eluded their pursuit, and at last took shelter between the gods themselves. They forbade it to be slain; and spoke in these words: "We are gods. This inhospitable village shall pay the penalty of its impiety; you alone shall go free from the chastisement. Quit your house, and come with us to the top of yonder hill."
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: nimble
sleepy
heavy
tame
items.explanation: 거위는 발과 날개를 이용해 노인들의 추격을 피했으므로 날렵하다는 말이 들어가야 한다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B와 C는 도망에 성공한 것과 맞지 않고, D는 잡히지 않은 상황과 어긋난다.

items.passage: White speaks of the spider "shooting out" the web, and such is the apparent feat, but doubtless the breeze assists in the operation. It is certainly taking good care of this floating banner from the loom of this little spinner upon our finger-tip. Longer and longer it grows. A yard or more of its length is soon swaying about in the breeze. So ______ has it now become that the little spider is visibly drawn upward, and now clings barely by his tip-toes. In another second he is off on his travels, where few could follow him even if they would.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: heavy
buoyant
tangled
fragile
items.explanation: 거미줄이 바람에 흔들리며 길어지고, 그 결과 작은 거미가 위로 끌려 올라간다. 따라서 공중에 뜨는 성질을 뜻하는 B가 정답이다. A는 위로 끌려간다는 결과와 반대이고, C와 D는 거미가 들려 올라가는 이유를 설명하지 못한다.

items.passage: Are the laws we have learned to be true for matter true also for mind? Matter we now know is ______; yet the form of it with which we once were so fondly familiar vanishes never to return. Is a like fate to be the lot of the soul? That mind should be capable of annihilation is as inconceivable as that matter should cease to be. Surely the spirit we feel existing round about us on every side now has been from ever, and will be for ever to come. But that portion of it which we each know as self, is it not like to a drop of rain seen in its falling through the air?
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: visible
temporary
indestructible
weightless
items.explanation: 뒤 문장에서 마음의 소멸은 물질이 존재하기를 멈추는 것만큼 상상할 수 없다고 한다. 따라서 물질은 파괴될 수 없다는 C가 정답이다. B는 이와 정반대이고, A와 D는 문맥의 핵심인 소멸 여부와 관련이 없다.

items.passage:
Glow-worms stood at the door to light them home, and as they passed in, the Fairy thought how charming it must be to dwell in such a lovely place. The floor of wax was pure and white as marble, while the walls were formed of golden honey-comb, and the air was ______ with the breath of flowers.

“You cannot see our Queen to-night,” said the little bee, “but I will show you to a bed where you can rest.”

And he led the tired Fairy to a little cell, where on a bed of flower-leaves he folded his wings and fell asleep.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: damp
silent
bitter
fragrant
items.explanation: 공기에 꽃의 숨결이 담겨 있다고 하고, 앞에서 집을 아름다운 곳으로 묘사한다. 따라서 향기롭다는 D가 정답이다. A와 C는 아름다운 분위기와 맞지 않고, B는 꽃의 숨결과 연결되지 않는다.

items.passage: Being thus installed as one of Mrs. Despard’s favorites, it was not at all singular that they should see a great deal of the young gentleman. And they did see him pretty often. Gradually he forgot his objection to meeting Lisbeth, and rather sneered in secret at the violence of that first shock of repulsion. It was all over, now, he said, and why should such a woman trouble him? Indeed, what greater proof of his security could he give himself than the fact that he could meet her almost daily, and still feel indifferent? It must be confessed that he rather prided himself upon his indifference.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone that occurs in the text?
options: from bitter resentment to open forgiveness of Lisbeth
from cheerful anticipation to sudden grief over a loss
from the man's confident reasoning to a quietly ironic remark
from fear of Lisbeth to growing romantic admiration for her
items.explanation: 지문 중반까지 청년은 Lisbeth를 매일 만나도 무관심하다며 자신이 안전하다고 자신 있게 생각한다. 그러나 마지막에 화자는 그가 그 무관심을 은근히 자랑스러워했다고 털어놓으며 그 자신감을 살짝 비꼰다. 따라서 C가 정답이고, A, B, D의 감정 변화는 지문에 나타나지 않는다.

items.passage:
I had looked forward to this quiet time as a schoolboy looks forward to the holidays, thinking at last I should have Fay to myself and could woo and win her back to me. But my hopes were doomed to disappointment. My darling seemed just as far from me as ever, only instead of being gay and laughter-loving she was quiet and depressed.

Annabel and I did all in our power to cheer her, but in vain. It was obvious that she was pining for society of her own age, and feeling the reaction after the gaiety of the Christmas vacation.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone that occurs in the text?
options: from deep sorrow to sudden relief
from open anger to calm acceptance
from dull boredom to lively excitement
from eager hope to quiet disappointment
items.explanation: 화자는 처음에 이 시간을 방학을 기다리는 학생처럼 기대하며 Fay의 마음을 되찾으려 했다. 그러나 곧 희망이 좌절되었다고 하고, 우울한 Fay를 위로해도 소용없었다고 말한다. 따라서 열띤 기대에서 실망으로 바뀌는 D가 정답이다.

items.passage:
The Judge took down his fiddle,
And put his feet on the stove,
And heaved a sigh from his middle
That might have been fat, or love;
He leaned his head on the mantel,
And bent his ear to the strings,
And the tender chords awakened
The echoes of many things.

The Bar had enjoyed the measure,
The Bench and Senate had been
Amused at the simple pleasure
He drew from his violin;
But weary of power and duty,
He had laid them down with a sigh,
Exhausted of life the beauty,
And he fiddled he knew not why.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone that occurs in the text?
options: from gently comic warmth to weary melancholy
from deep grief to triumphant celebration
from open anger to light amusement
from stiff formality to sharp mockery
items.explanation: 첫 연은 판사가 난로에 발을 올리고 살찐 탓인지 사랑 탓인지 모를 한숨을 쉬는 등 유머러스하고 따뜻하다. 둘째 연에서는 권력과 의무에 지쳐 삶의 아름다움이 다했다는 쓸쓸한 분위기로 바뀐다. 따라서 A가 정답이고, B, C, D의 변화는 지문과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage:
ELSIE.

No, that's too rough. We'll play husband and wife. Bob and I will get married, and, Teresa, you must be the minister and a bridesmaid.

(_They retire into the house, where, with the aid of a wrapper, a night dress, a bouquet, and a black mackintosh, the ceremony is properly performed._)

ELSIE.

Now we'll have a little girl baby, and (_to Teresa_) you must be it.

TERESA.

No, I want to be the wife now, and you be the baby.

ELSIE.

No, I'll be the husband, and let Bob be the baby.

BOB.

I won't be the baby!
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone that occurs in the text?
options: from a bitter quarrel to friendly agreement
from cooperative play to petty arguing

items.explanation: 처음에 아이들은 결혼 놀이를 함께 하며 의식을 제대로 치른다. 그러나 아기 역할을 정하는 대목에서 Teresa와 Bob이 서로 원하지 않는 역할을 거부하며 다툰다. 따라서 협력하는 놀이에서 사소한 말다툼으로 바뀌는 B가 정답이다.
